---
title: "Paintbox: components versus clusters"
subtitle: "Catalog P-03, P-04 · rung 3 · after Broderick (MLSS 2016, part I)"
description: "A Dirichlet draw with a thousand tiny weights, hit by uniform drops: many components, few clusters, and new clusters ever more rarely."
toc: false
---

Take a Dirichlet draw with many components and a small parameter: K = 1000 and a = 0.01.
Lay its weights side by side on the unit interval. A handful of pieces are wide and the
rest are slivers too thin to see. Now drop points uniformly on the interval, one unit at a
time. Each drop lands in some piece; the pieces that have been hit are the *clusters*, and
there are far fewer of them than *components*.

```{=html}
<div id="w-paintbox" class="dpx-host column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/paintbox.js"></script>
<script>
  window.__dpxPaintbox = DPX["paintbox"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("w-paintbox"), {});
</script>
```

## What to try

- **Drop 1, Drop 10, Drop 100.** After 100 drops only a couple of dozen of the 1000 pieces
  are blue (the exact expectation for K = 1000 and a = 0.01 is 24.2). The staircase below
  records, for every drop, whether it hit a piece seen before or a new one; the steps get
  further and further apart.
- **log x.** On a log scale of the drop number the staircase is close to a straight line:
  clusters grow like alpha log N, with alpha = K·a.
- **K and a.** Keep K·a fixed (say K = 5000 and a = 0.002, K·a = 10) and the picture barely
  changes: that limit is the Dirichlet process with concentration alpha = K·a. Lower a to
  0.001 (K·a = 1) and a few pieces take almost everything.
- **Hover** over the bar (or use the piece picker) to read a piece's weight rho_k.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Components are the infinitely many atoms of the model; clusters are the ones the J units
actually occupy. On this site K_J always counts clusters: the number of fitted components
among the J units. After Broderick (MLSS 2016, part I, demos 3 and 4); the mathematics is
re-implemented and no code is copied.
:::

Standalone version: [embed/paintbox.html](../../embed/paintbox.html), for example
`?n=100` or `?K=5000&a=0.002&n=200`.
